title.title: The Correspondence of Esther Roberts Hunt Collins

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of Quaker minister Esther Roberts Hunt Collins is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: Thou mayst see I gave Hannah Warrington paper when here to write & as there is some blank, write on that.

Now my dear child, I may likewise inform I received letters from Caleb, Nathan, also thine, which were acceptable. Thee queries about my getting home from Philadelphia, I rode up with J. Roberts & Wife after going to the Monthly Meeting with Mary Borton & & and had cause for thankfulness, that our way was made so easy for thy return back to the school & mine home, where thy Father affectionately received me. Esther Warrington continues very poorly, & the Doctor thinks her complaints dangerous. Our dear relation Elizabeth Collins desires her love to thee. O, my dear child, mayst thou walk worthy of the love & tender regard of thy friends, as thou hast many. Joseph Justice also desired his love inserted, & many more do love thee & would be grieved to hear anything bad of thee. Hence it is needful for thee to be exceedingly careful how thee conducts thyself, and guard against everything which is hurtful.
Praying in the secret of thy heart for preservation out of the many snares there is in this world, one of which is giddy, light conversation, which I want to guard against.

closer.salute: Thy Father united with me in love to thee, Mary P. also
